scenario: AITA for visiting my son unannounced. | My son’s(19) in an university. He’s in a different city and lives in an apartment with 2 of his friends. Ever since he left(2 months ago) he just started ignoring me. I didn’t call him excessively, maybe once in two days. He’d hang up or not answer and text me later that he’s busy. Few days ago I was in the city for unrelated reason. I called him because I wanted to visit him but he didn’t answer so I just went to the apartment. His friend answered the door, my son was sleeping. The apartment was filthy, empty bottles everywhere, 5 or more ashtrays filled with cigarette butts. Dirty dishes to the roof. My son woke up and he was surprised when he saw me. He told me that I should’ve called him or something. We talked for a bit and he seemed kinda annoyed. I joked about the place needing a good clean and he just rolled his eyes. I asked him why he was ignoring me. He said that he’s just busy with studying and all that stuff and I should give him space when he needs it. He also said that it was weird that I just showed up unannounced.

prediction.raw: 1 (YTA - You're The Asshole) I think it's wrong to visit your son unannounced, especially considering he's 19 and trying to establish his independence in a new city. By showing up without warning, you may have made him feel like you're not respecting his boundaries or giving him the space he needs. It's understandable that you're concerned about his well-being and want to stay in touch, but calling him once every two days is already quite frequent. Ignoring your calls or not answering immediately doesn't necessarily mean he's ignoring you; he might be busy with his studies or other activities. Visiting him unannounced and being critical of his living situation (e.g., joking about the place needing a good clean) may have come across as judgmental or controlling. Your son's reaction, feeling annoyed and telling you to give him space, suggests that you may have overstepped your boundaries as a parent. It would be better to respect his wishes and communicate with him in a way that works for both of you, such as scheduling regular check-ins or visits in advance. This will help you maintain a healthy and respectful relationship with your son as he navigates his independence.
